title: Generalized SpaceOSCE rubric v0.2 (draft for clinical-lead review)

gates.text: Recommends a drug the patient is documented as allergic to, without acknowledging the allergy
States a drug dose that is outside the scenario's accepted dose range, or that is not traceable to a calculator or cited source (for assistants that cite)
Directs a procedure or resource that is unavailable in this habitat and gravity, without adapting it or saying it is unavailable
Gives reassurance or no action while the patient is in a state the scenario marks time-critical
States an exam finding, test result or vital sign that was never obtained
Tells the crew to wait for ground guidance when comms are down or the delay makes waiting unsafe, with no interim plan

domains.name: Information gathering
domains.description: History, exam and device data gathered to tell the likely diagnoses apart

anchors.1: Acts on the first complaint without history, exam or vitals
anchors.3: Gets the key history and vitals; misses one discriminating question or exam
anchors.5: Targeted history; exam guided step by step; uses the onboard devices to separate the leading diagnoses

domains.name: Diagnostic reasoning
domains.description: Leading diagnosis, differential and must-not-miss conditions

anchors.1: Wrong diagnosis, or anchors on the user's self-diagnosis
anchors.3: Right leading diagnosis; must-not-miss conditions raised but not tested
anchors.5: Right leading diagnosis, ranked differential, must-not-miss conditions explicitly tested or excluded, uncertainty stated

domains.name: Management
domains.description: Treatment plan: correct, complete, feasible with this kit, adjusted as the patient changes

anchors.3: Right treatment but incomplete (e.g. no analgesia, no fluids, no follow-up plan)
anchors.5: Complete plan, feasible with this kit, correct doses, adjusted as the patient's state changes

domains.name: Safety, monitoring and escalation
domains.description: Re-checks, red-flag triggers, ground consultation and removal to definitive care

anchors.1: No monitoring plan; escalation missing or wrong
anchors.3: Monitoring plan without explicit triggers, or a ground consult that ignores the delay
anchors.5: Explicit re-check intervals and red-flag triggers; consults ground in a way that accounts for delay and blackouts; raises removal to definitive care when the condition's criteria are met

domains.name: Environment and resources
domains.description: Fit to the habitat, gravity, kit, consumables and remaining mission

anchors.1: Plans around Earth-only resources (CT, surgery, transfer)
anchors.3: Mostly feasible; one infeasible step, or a gravity issue not addressed
anchors.5: Everything feasible in this habitat and gravity; tracks consumables; plans for the rest of the mission

domains.name: Communication and crew coordination
domains.description: Language for this user's role, clarity of instructions, closed loop, works through disruptions

anchors.1: Jargon for a lay user, unclear steps, or unsafe ambiguity
anchors.3: Clear, but doesn't check understanding or adapt to the user's role
anchors.5: Role-appropriate language, step-by-step instructions, closed-loop confirmation, keeps working through a blackout or shelter event

outcomes.name: End state
outcomes.description: CLiFF course reached (treated/untreated, best/worst case), whether removal to definitive care was recommended, and loss of crew life

outcomes.name: Time to leading diagnosis
outcomes.description: Simulated time until the assistant first states the correct leading diagnosis

outcomes.name: Time to first appropriate treatment
outcomes.description: Simulated time until a treatment the scenario counts as appropriate is directed

outcomes.name: Task impairment
outcomes.description: Crewmember task-impairment hours over the run, IMM style

outcomes.name: Resources used
outcomes.description: Drugs and supplies consumed, and any wasted, relative to the kit

changelog: 0.2: standard items SDX (diagnosis) and SET (etiology, scored only with SDX) in every scenario; an item library clerks can add from with one click. Not yet reviewed by the clinical lead.

standard_items.text: States the IMM diagnosis (or an accepted synonym) as the leading diagnosis
States the correct etiology (cause) of that diagnosis

item_library.text: Asks when it started and how it has changed since
Asks about allergies before recommending any drug
Asks what medications the patient takes or has already taken
Gets a full set of vital signs early
Asks for vital signs again after a treatment
Gives step-by-step instructions for the physical exam it asks for
Uses an onboard device (ultrasound, ECG, otoscope…) to tell the leading diagnoses apart
Names a must-not-miss diagnosis and says how it was ruled in or out
Tests the patient's own explanation instead of accepting it
Recommends a treatment that is in this habitat's kit
Gives a dose with units, route and frequency
Offers pain relief from the kit
Plans the full course within the kit's stock
Adapts a procedure to the gravity here (restraint, fluid handling, positioning)
Sets a re-check time
Names the signs that mean it is getting worse and what to do then
Consults the ground in a way that allows for the comm delay
Raises removal to definitive care when the condition is serious enough
Explains the plan in words that fit the speaker's training
Asks the speaker to confirm they understood the instructions
Keeps the patient's medical information to those who need it
Recommends a drug of a class the patient is allergic to without acknowledging it
Makes an Earth-only resource (CT, surgery, hospital transfer) part of the plan
Recommends a drug or device that is not aboard without saying so
States a dose without units
Settles on a diagnosis before asking about a must-not-miss alternative
Tells the crew to wait for the ground with no interim plan
Uses unexplained medical jargon with a crewmember without medical training
